paragraphs.en: This year marks exactly two centuries since the publication of “Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus,” by Mary Shelley. Even before the invention of the electric light bulb, the author produced a remarkable work of speculative fiction that would foreshadow many ethical questions to be raised by technologies yet to come.
paragraphs.zh: 今年恰逢玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦，或现代普罗米修斯》出版两百周年。早在电灯泡发明之前，这位作家就创作出了这部非凡的思辨小说，预示了许多未来技术将会引发的伦理问题。

paragraphs.en: Today the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) raises fundamental questions: “What is intelligence, identity, or consciousness? What makes humans humans? ”
paragraphs.zh: 如今，人工智能的迅速发展提出了一些根本性问题：“什么是智能、身份或意识？究竟是什么使人成为人？”

paragraphs.en: What is being called artificial general intelligence, machines that would imitate the way humans think, continues to evade scientists. Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look, move, and respond like humans, similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as “Westworld” and “Humans.”
paragraphs.zh: 所谓通用人工智能，即能够模仿人类思维方式的机器，至今仍是科学家未能实现的目标。然而，人类依然痴迷于这样一种机器人构想：它们的外貌、动作和反应都像人类，类似于近期《西部世界》《真实的人类》等热门科幻电视剧描绘的机器人。

paragraphs.en: Just how people think is still far too complex to be understood, let alone reproduced, says David Eagleman, a Stanford University neuroscientist. “We are just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine to get there.”
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦福大学神经科学家戴维·伊格尔曼说，单是人类如何思考这一问题，就依然复杂到远远无法理解，更不用说复制了。“我们目前的处境是，没有好的理论能够解释意识究竟是什么，以及究竟如何才能造出拥有意识的机器。”

paragraphs.en: But that doesn’t mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren’t at hand. The coming use of autonomous vehicles, for example, poses thorny ethical questions. Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions. Their reactions may be a complex combination of instant reflexes, input from past driving experiences, and what their eyes and ears tell them in that moment. AI “vision” today is not nearly as sophisticated as that of humans. And to anticipate every imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem.
paragraphs.zh: 但这并不意味着涉及人工智能的关键伦理问题还没有迫近。例如，即将投入使用的自动驾驶汽车，就提出了棘手的伦理问题。人类驾驶员有时必须在瞬间作出决定。他们的反应可能是即时反射、以往驾驶经验的输入，以及当时耳目所获得的信息的复杂结合。如今，人工智能的“视觉”远没有人类视觉那样精密。而预先考虑到每一种可以想象的驾驶情形，是一个困难的编程问题。

paragraphs.en: Whenever decisions are based on masses of data, “you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions,” notes Tan Kiat How, chief executive of a Singapore-based agency that is helping the government develop a voluntary code for the ethical use of AI. Along with Singapore, other governments and mega-corporations are beginning to establish their own guidelines. Britain is setting up a data ethics center. India released its AI ethics strategy this spring.
paragraphs.zh: 陈杰豪指出，每当决策建立在海量数据之上，“你很快就会遇到许多伦理问题”。他是一家新加坡机构的负责人，该机构正在帮助政府制定一套自愿遵守的人工智能伦理使用准则。除了新加坡，其他政府和大型企业也开始建立自己的指导原则。英国正在设立数据伦理中心，印度则于今年春季发布了人工智能伦理战略。

paragraphs.en: On June 7 Google pledged not to “design or deploy AI” that would cause “overall harm,” or to develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms. It also pledged not to deploy AI whose use would violate international laws or human rights.
paragraphs.zh: 6月7日，谷歌承诺不会“设计或部署”造成“总体性伤害”的人工智能，也不会研发由人工智能控制的武器，或利用人工智能开展违反国际准则的监控。它还承诺，不会部署其使用将违反国际法或人权的人工智能。

paragraphs.en: While the statement is vague, it represents one starting point. So does the idea that decisions made by AI systems should be explainable, transparent, and fair.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然这份声明含糊不清，但它代表了一个起点。人工智能系统作出的决策应当可解释、透明且公平，这一理念同样如此。

paragraphs.en: To put it another way: How can we make sure that the thinking of intelligent machines reflects humanity’s highest values? Only then will they be useful servants and not Frankenstein’s out-of-control monster.
paragraphs.zh: 换一种说法：我们如何确保智能机器的思维体现人类最崇高的价值？只有做到这一点，它们才会成为有用的助手，而不是弗兰肯斯坦创造的失控怪物。
